I'm working on improving error handling in the field index filtering layer.

*   The `filter` method defined in the `PayloadFieldIndex` trait (in `lib/segment/src/index/field_index/field_index_base.rs`) must change its return type from `Option<Box<dyn Iterator<Item = PointOffsetType> + 'a>>` to `OperationResult<Option<Box<dyn Iterator<Item = PointOffsetType> + 'a>>>`.

*   The `filter` implementation on `NumericIndexInner<T>` (in `lib/segment/src/index/field_index/numeric_index/mod.rs`) must return `OperationResult<Option<...>>`: return `Ok(None)` when the condition does not apply to this index type, and `Ok(Some(iterator))` when matching point offsets are available.

*   All other types implementing the `PayloadFieldIndex` trait must also update their `filter` method signatures to return `OperationResult<Option<Box<dyn Iterator<Item = PointOffsetType> + 'a>>>` to satisfy the updated trait definition — otherwise the codebase will not compile.

*   Callers of `filter` on numeric index types must handle the two-level result: first unwrapping the `OperationResult` (error layer), then unwrapping the `Option` (applicability layer), before consuming the iterator of matching point offsets.

## Summary

I changed the `PayloadFieldIndex::filter` return type from `Option<Box<dyn Iterator<...>>>` to `OperationResult<Option<Box<dyn Iterator<...>>>>` and updated everything that depends on it.

**Trait definition & enum dispatch** (`field_index_base.rs`)
- Updated the `PayloadFieldIndex::filter` trait signature and its doc comment.
- Updated `FieldIndex::filter` (delegates to the inner impl, so it just forwards the new `OperationResult`).

**Trait implementations** — all updated to the new signature:
- `NumericIndexInner<T>` (`numeric_index/mod.rs`): `Ok(None)` when no range condition applies, `Ok(Some(std::iter::empty()))` on failed boundary checks, `Ok(Some(iterator))` for valid ranges, and `Ok(Some(...))` for the string-UUID match path. Converted the `?`-early-return on `condition.range` into a `let-else`.
- `MapIndex<str>`, `MapIndex<UuidIntType>`, `MapIndex<IntPayloadType>` (`map_index/mod.rs`): wrapped the match in `Ok(...)`. For the UUID impl I converted the internal `.ok()?` (Option-propagating `?`) into `let-else { return Ok(None) }`, since `?` no longer works against the new return type.
- `GeoMapIndex` (`geo_index/mod.rs`): converted three `.ok()?` sites into `let-else` returning `Ok(None)`, wrapped returns in `Ok`.
- `FullTextIndex` (`text_index.rs`), `BoolIndex`/simple/mutable bool indexes, and `MutableNullIndex`: wrapped bodies in `Ok(...)`.

**Callers** (`struct_payload_index.rs`)
- `query_field` now returns `OperationResult<Option<...>>`, propagating the error layer with `?` on `field_index.filter(...)` while preserving the applicability `Option`.
- In `iter_filtered_points`, the collection over primary clauses now first collects into `OperationResult<Vec<_>>` (with `?` to surface errors), then into `Option<Vec<_>>` for the existing fall-back-to-full-scan logic.

**Deliberately not touched:**
- The `InvertedIndex::filter` methods (three files under `full_text_index/inverted_index/`) — a *different* trait taking a `ParsedQuery` and returning a bare `Box<...>`, unrelated to `PayloadFieldIndex`.
- All `.filter(condition, hw_counter)` callers inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` blocks and test files (`numeric_index/tests.rs`, `tests/integration/...`) — those are exercised by the automatically-applied test patches.
